From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)
Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims
is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the
Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or
public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.
Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing
bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter
and is not expected to be material.
Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course
operating costs.
Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime
above.
Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject
to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft
Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or
on-costs apply.
6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external
email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity
timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised
person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation
remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no
loss amount.

Buyer has completed its own verification.
11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer
must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline

The Seller's cover note describes several open risks as resolved, but its own Disclosure Letter says they are not. Bluefen "is addressed", yet no consent has been delivered. Riverlark will be released "following Completion", yet the facility has not been repaid. DD-006 is "not expected to be material", yet the investigation is preliminary. The Sandbar renewals are "ordinary-course", but the disclosure says nothing about that. On top of this, the limitation package would cap or erode almost every route we have to recover loss for those same risks.

We should not treat any characterisation in the cover note as a representation. Each one is either unsupported or contradicted by the Disclosure Letter. If the Seller wants us to rely on them, it should give them as warranties.

**Timing:** the disclosure is stated as at 22 September 2026. That is about six weeks old today (6 November 2026). We need a brought-down Disclosure Letter, and the Seller should not be able to cure warranty breaches through updated disclosure before Completion.

---

## Part A: Deal-critical issues (resolve before signing)

### 1. Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m): release "following Completion" is not debt-free

- **Why it matters:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release means we own the company while the security is still registered and the debt is still outstanding. The change-control clause in DD-003 (cl 8.1) may also trigger a default or acceleration at Completion.
- **Position:**
  - The facility is repaid at Completion out of the price, under a payoff letter that confirms the exact payout figure.
  - Riverlark delivers a deed of release at Completion, with PPSR financing change statements and discharges of any other registered security.
  - Riverlark gives a waiver of cl 8.1 for the period between signing and Completion.
  - The payout figure, including break costs, accrued interest and fees, is defined as Indebtedness and deducted dollar-for-dollar.
  - These are Completion deliverables, not post-Completion covenants.
- **Also check** whether the Seller has granted security over the Paperbark shares themselves. See item 9.

### 2. Bluefen consent (~30% of revenue): weak condition

- **Why it matters:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue. The proposal has two weaknesses:
  - "Reasonable endeavours" is a low obligation.
  - Treating the condition as "satisfied on delivery of written consent" ignores the separate conditions in DD-002 cl 11.3. A consent could be delivered while those conditions are unmet, or the consent itself could be qualified.
- **Position:**
  - The Condition Precedent requires an unconditional written consent under cl 11.2, in a form acceptable to the Buyer (acting reasonably).
  - It also requires evidence that every cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied, or a waiver of those conditions.
  - The consent must not vary pricing, term or termination rights.
  - The Seller gives a "best endeavours" or "all reasonable endeavours" obligation.
  - Only the Buyer can waive the condition, and there is a clear long-stop date and termination right.
  - Consider a price adjustment or earn-out protection if Bluefen terminates or materially changes terms within, say, 12 months.

### 3. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applied to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

- **Why it matters:** The default in cl 12.3 ("any limitation … applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise") reverses the usual position. Unless each carve-out is drafted expressly, the cap, basket, time limit and disclosure qualifications would apply to:
  - specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, tax);
  - covenants;
  - leakage and price-adjustment claims;
  - title claims;
  - potentially fraud.
- **Position:** The limitations apply only to claims for breach of the general Warranties. Express carve-outs from all limitations should cover:
  - fraud, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment;
  - the Title and Capacity Warranties;
  - the Tax Warranties and tax indemnity, which get their own regime;
  - specific indemnities;
  - covenant and Completion obligations;
  - price adjustment and leakage.
- **On non-reliance:** It must not exclude fraud. We should not accept it as a bar to claims for misleading or deceptive conduct about matters in the Disclosure Letter or cover note. Under NSW law, liability for fraud cannot be excluded, and Australian Consumer Law s 18 claims are not reliably excluded by non-reliance clauses. Even so, the drafting should be clean.
- **On exclusive remedy:** Preserve termination rights before Completion, specific performance and injunctive relief.

### 4. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging (cl 8.3) and general disclosure (Schedule 7, DL 1.1–1.2)

- **Why it matters:** Together, these provisions mean anything in the data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers or "publicly searchable" records, or anything "discoverable" by us or our advisers, defeats a claim. That would undercut almost all warranty protection, including on the very issues flagged here.
- **Position:**
  - Delete cl 8.3, or limit it to actual knowledge of specific named deal-team members, of the specific breach, as at signing.
  - Expressly exclude constructive or imputed knowledge and the knowledge of advisers.
  - The warranties are given notwithstanding any due diligence.
  - Disclosure must be fair, specific and against identified warranties, with enough detail for us to assess nature and scope.
  - Delete DL 1.1–1.2 as general disclosures. At most, accept the data room index as context but not as disclosure.
  - Add three exclusions from any disclosure:
    - Disclosure does not qualify the Title, Capacity or Tax Warranties, or any indemnity.
    - The Disclosure Letter is not itself warranted as complete; the Seller should warrant that it is accurate.
    - DL 1.4 ("no admission") must not reduce the effect of what is disclosed.

### 5. Title and capacity: same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity"

- **Why it matters:** If we do not get good title to 100% of the shares, we have lost the whole AUD 24m. A 20% cap and an 18-month limit are not acceptable for that risk.
- **Position:**
  - Title and Capacity are Fundamental Warranties, capped at 100% of the price.
  - Claims can be brought for a longer period, for example 6–7 years. That reflects the limitation period for contract claims in NSW.
  - No de minimis, no basket, and no disclosure against them.
  - A share register (DD-012) is not proof of title. See item 9.

---

## Part B: Specific risk items needing specific protection

### 6. Ironquay IP (SOW3): indemnity limited to "the payment" is inadequate

- **Why it matters:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials only transfer on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 still open. The data room has no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
  - If the fees are unpaid, Paperbark may not own IP it uses.
  - Our exposure then includes infringement claims, re-development or licensing costs, and customer impacts. It is not just AUD 180k.
  - The DL itself notes that DD-010 is not bank verification.
- **Position:**
  - **Completion deliverable:** the Seller produces bank evidence that all SOW3 fees are paid, plus a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay.
  - **If those are unavailable:** a specific indemnity covering all Losses from any defect in Paperbark's title to the SOW3 materials. This includes third-party claims and the cost of getting a licence or rebuilding.
  - The indemnity sits outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with a time limit of at least 6 years.
  - It is supported by a retention or escrow.
- Ask whether any other Ironquay SOWs contain a similar clause.

### 7. DD-006 export/privacy incident: "not expected to be material" is unsupported

- **Why it matters:**
  - A download link went to an unintended external address. It may cover around 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). That is personal information.
  - Paperbark's turnover appears to be about AUD 12m, implied by Bluefen being about AUD 3.6m and 30% of revenue. That is well above the small business exemption, so Paperbark is likely an APP entity under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).
  - Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days of becoming aware of it.
  - The investigation was still "preliminary" at 22 September. We do not know when the incident occurred, so the assessment deadline may already have been missed. That is a compliance exposure in itself.
  - There may also be contractual notification obligations to customers (possibly Bluefen), regulatory exposure (including civil penalties since the 2022 amendments), and reputational risk.
- **Position:**
  - **Information request:** incident date and awareness date; the investigation report; access logs showing whether the link was opened or downloaded; link expiry; any confirmation from the recipient that the file was deleted; the NDB assessment and decision; any customer-contract notification requirements; whether this has happened before.
  - **Pre-Completion covenant:** complete the assessment with competent advisers, make any required notifications, and keep the Buyer informed with consultation rights.
  - **Specific indemnity:** cover regulatory, notification, remediation, third-party and customer-contract losses. It sits outside the general cap and basket and is not qualified by disclosure.
  - Tighten the privacy and data-security warranties.
  - Consider a retention.
- If the Seller is confident this is immaterial, it should be willing to warrant that position.

### 8. DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000): excluded from the funds flow

- **Why it matters:** These bonuses are transaction costs triggered by the sale. Leaving them out of the funds flow pushes them onto us after Completion, which goes against debt-free/cash-free pricing.
  - On-costs are also unaddressed. These include NSW payroll tax (currently 5.45%, if Paperbark is above the threshold), possibly superannuation guarantee (currently 12%, depending on whether the bonuses are ordinary time earnings), PAYG withholding and workers' compensation.
  - Rough total cost is likely AUD 450k–500k. This needs payroll verification.
  - The continued-employment conditions may mean some amounts fall due after Completion.
- **Position:**
  - Define the bonuses and all associated on-costs as Transaction Costs or Indebtedness, deducted from the price.
  - Pay them through payroll at or immediately after Completion, using funds the Seller provides.
  - Any amounts paid later are held in escrow or retained.
  - Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall and for any other change-of-control or retention payments.
  - Correct the funds flow before signing.

### 9. Title evidence (DD-012)

- **Why it matters:** The DL itself says DD-012 is only the source the Seller relies on, and that we have not completed our own verification.
- **Our verification:**
  - Search ASIC company records and compare them with the register.
  - Review the constitution, any shareholders' agreement, pre-emptive rights and transfer restrictions.
  - Confirm there are no options, convertible notes, ESOP grants or share rights. This is relevant given the employee bonuses.
  - Run a PPSR search against the Seller for any security over the shares, and check Riverlark specifically.
  - Review the issue history.
- **Completion deliverables:**
  - executed share transfers;
  - share certificates, or an indemnity for any lost certificates;
  - releases of any encumbrance over the shares;
  - waivers of pre-emptive rights;
  - board resolutions approving the transfer.

### 10. Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000)

- **Why it matters:** The DL describes three *related* renewals and asks that they be "read together for timing/scope". This suggests one arrangement split into three. That pattern can be used to stay under a material-contract threshold or a conduct-of-business approval threshold.
  - The disclosure does not say the renewals are ordinary-course, unavoidable, terminable or accrued. The Seller's cover note claims they are without support.
- **Position:** Ask for:
  - the dates entered into, and whether they fall after any conduct-of-business restriction began;
  - who approved them, and whether any related party is involved;
  - term, termination rights and prepayments;
  - business justification.
- Depending on the answers:
  - treat the renewals as a single Material Contract;
  - treat any unnecessary or uncommercial commitment as debt-like, a price reduction, or a Seller-funded termination;
  - confirm conduct-of-business covenants aggregate related transactions.

### 11. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"

- **Not accepted.** We need:
  - a standalone tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, including secondary liabilities;
  - Tax Warranties outside the general cap, or with a cap at the price, and a time limit of at least the ATO amendment period plus a margin (around 5–7 years, and unlimited for fraud or evasion);
  - no disclosure against the tax indemnity;
  - conduct-of-claims provisions.
- **IP:** Given Ironquay, the IP ownership warranties should have at least an extended time limit and a higher cap. Consider making core IP ownership fundamental.

---

## Part C: General warranty economics (negotiable)

| Term | Seller | Comment | Buyer counter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap (general) | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Within market range only if specific risks are carved out and specifically indemnified | 30–50%, or accept 20% *only* with full carve-outs in Parts A–B; consider W&I insurance |
| De minimis | AUD 25k | About 0.1% of the price; workable | AUD 10–15k; related claims aggregate for de minimis |
| Basket | AUD 250k, **deductible** (excess only) | Deductible basket favours the Seller | **Tipping** basket (recover from first dollar once exceeded) at about AUD 120–240k; claims below the de minimis still count toward it |
| Time limit (general) | 18 months | Gives one full audit cycle; at the lower end | 24 months; Fundamental 6–7 yrs; Tax per item 11 |

If the Seller insists on a low cap and short time limit, W&I insurance becomes worth considering. Excluded known risks (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark) would still need specific Seller indemnities, because W&I policies exclude known matters.

---

## Part D: Lower priority but confirm

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification only, on the Seller's reading. Our counsel should confirm against the lease text, including any change-in-control termination right. Add a covenant that the Seller gives notice on time.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Only an assignment restriction, on the Seller's reading. Confirm the clause has no change-of-control or "deemed assignment" wording.
- **Security for indemnities:** Seek a retention or escrow covering the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonus balance). The Seller is presumably a holding vehicle, so we may otherwise be left with an empty Seller. Also seek a parent guarantee if applicable.

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the cover-note characterisations.** Bluefen is not "addressed", Riverlark is not debt-free, and DD-006 and Sandbar are unsupported. Require warranties if the Seller wants us to rely on them.
2. **Riverlark:** payoff letter, repayment from the price, and deed of release plus PPSR discharges *at* Completion. Payout defined as Indebtedness. Waiver of cl 8.1.
3. **Bluefen:** unconditional consent and cl 11.3 satisfied as a Buyer-only waivable CP. Best or all reasonable endeavours. Long-stop date. Consider price protection.
4. **Limitations:** apply only to general Warranty Claims. Carve out fraud, Fundamental and Tax Warranties, indemnities, covenants and leakage. Reverse the cl 12.3 default.
5. **Delete cl 8.3 and the general disclosures.** Specific, fair disclosure only. No disclosure against Fundamental or Tax Warranties or indemnities. Bring-down at Completion with no cure.
6. **Title and Capacity:** fundamental, 100% cap, 6–7 years. Independent title checks and Completion deliverables.
7. **Ironquay:** payment evidence plus confirmatory assignment at Completion. Otherwise a full uncapped IP indemnity with retention.
8. **DD-006:** information request now, pre-Completion NDB covenant, specific indemnity and retention. Flag the possibly missed 30-day assessment deadline.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus all on-costs treated as Transaction Costs, deducted from the price. Correct the funds flow.
10. **Sandbar:** diligence the split renewals. Treat them as one contract. Price or terminate if not genuinely ordinary course.
11. **Tax:** standalone tax indemnity and a separate limitation regime.
12. **Economics:** tipping basket, a modest de minimis, a 24-month time limit. Either a higher cap or 20% only with full carve-outs. Consider W&I insurance.
13. **Updated Disclosure Letter** as at a current date, plus a retention or escrow to back the specific indemnities.

**Caveats:** This review is based only on the Seller's cover note and Disclosure Letter. We have not seen the full SPA text or the underlying DD documents (DD-002 to DD-012). The clause readings above should be checked against those documents. Statutory rates and thresholds (payroll tax, super guarantee, NDB timing) should be confirmed by the relevant specialists before we rely on figures.

- **Why it matters:**
  - A download link went to an unintended external address. It may cover around 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). That is personal information.
  - Paperbark's turnover appears to be about AUD 12m, implied by Bluefen being about AUD 3.6m and 30% of revenue. That is well above the small business exemption, so Paperbark is likely an APP entity under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).
  - Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days of becoming aware of it.
  - The investigation was still "preliminary" at 22 September. We do not know when the incident occurred, so the assessment deadline may already have been missed. That is a compliance exposure in itself.
  - There may also be contractual notification obligations to customers (possibly Bluefen), regulatory exposure (including civil penalties since the 2022 amendments), and reputational risk.
- **Position:**
  - **Information request:** incident date and awareness date; the investigation report; access logs showing whether the link was opened or downloaded; link expiry; any confirmation from the recipient that the file was deleted; the NDB assessment and decision; any customer-contract notification requirements; whether this has happened before.
  - **Pre-Completion covenant:** complete the assessment with competent advisers, make any required notifications, and keep the Buyer informed with consultation rights.
  - **Specific indemnity:** cover regulatory, notification, remediation, third-party and customer-contract losses. It sits outside the general cap and basket and is not qualified by disclosure.
  - Tighten the privacy and data-security warranties.
  - Consider a retention.
- If the Seller is confident this is immaterial, it should be willing to warrant that position.

### 8. DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000): excluded from the funds flow

- **Why it matters:** These bonuses are transaction costs triggered by the sale. Leaving them out of the funds flow pushes them onto us after Completion, which goes against debt-free/cash-free pricing.
  - On-costs are also unaddressed. These include NSW payroll tax (currently 5.45%, if Paperbark is above the threshold), possibly superannuation guarantee (currently 12%, depending on whether the bonuses are ordinary time earnings), PAYG withholding and workers' compensation.
  - Rough total cost is likely AUD 450k–500k. This needs payroll verification.
  - The continued-employment conditions may mean some amounts fall due after Completion.
- **Position:**
  - Define the bonuses and all associated on-costs as Transaction Costs or Indebtedness, deducted from the price.
  - Pay them through payroll at or immediately after Completion, using funds the Seller provides.
  - Any amounts paid later are held in escrow or retained.
  - Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall and for any other change-of-control or retention payments.
  - Correct the funds flow before signing.

### 9. Title evidence (DD-012)

- **Why it matters:** The DL itself says DD-012 is only the source the Seller relies on, and that we have not completed our own verification.
- **Our verification:**
  - Search ASIC company records and compare them with the register.
  - Review the constitution, any shareholders' agreement, pre-emptive rights and transfer restrictions.
  - Confirm there are no options, convertible notes, ESOP grants or share rights. This is relevant given the employee bonuses.
  - Run a PPSR search against the Seller for any security over the shares, and check Riverlark specifically.
  - Review the issue history.
- **Completion deliverables:**
  - executed share transfers;
  - share certificates, or an indemnity for any lost certificates;
  - releases of any encumbrance over the shares;
  - waivers of pre-emptive rights;
  - board resolutions approving the transfer.

### 10. Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000)

- **Why it matters:** The DL describes three *related* renewals and asks that they be "read together for timing/scope". This suggests one arrangement split into three. That pattern can be used to stay under a material-contract threshold or a conduct-of-business approval threshold.
  - The disclosure does not say the renewals are ordinary-course, unavoidable, terminable or accrued. The Seller's cover note claims they are without support.
- **Position:** Ask for:
  - the dates entered into, and whether they fall after any conduct-of-business restriction began;
  - who approved them, and whether any related party is involved;
  - term, termination rights and prepayments;
  - business justification.
- Depending on the answers:
  - treat the renewals as a single Material Contract;
  - treat any unnecessary or uncommercial commitment as debt-like, a price reduction, or a Seller-funded termination;
  - confirm conduct-of-business covenants aggregate related transactions.

### 11. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"

- **Not accepted.** We need:
  - a standalone tax indemnity covering pre-Completion tax, including secondary liabilities;
  - Tax Warranties outside the general cap, or with a cap at the price, and a time limit of at least the ATO amendment period plus a margin (around 5–7 years, and unlimited for fraud or evasion);
  - no disclosure against the tax indemnity;
  - conduct-of-claims provisions.
- **IP:** Given Ironquay, the IP ownership warranties should have at least an extended time limit and a higher cap. Consider making core IP ownership fundamental.

## Part C: General warranty economics (negotiable)

| Term | Seller | Comment | Buyer counter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cap (general) | 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Within market range only if specific risks are carved out and specifically indemnified | 30–50%, or accept 20% *only* with full carve-outs in Parts A–B; consider W&I insurance |
| De minimis | AUD 25k | About 0.1% of the price; workable | AUD 10–15k; related claims aggregate for de minimis |
| Basket | AUD 250k, **deductible** (excess only) | Deductible basket favours the Seller | **Tipping** basket (recover from first dollar once exceeded) at about AUD 120–240k; claims below the de minimis still count toward it |
| Time limit (general) | 18 months | Gives one full audit cycle; at the lower end | 24 months; Fundamental 6–7 yrs; Tax per item 11 |

If the Seller insists on a low cap and short time limit, W&I insurance becomes worth considering. Excluded known risks (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark) would still need specific Seller indemnities, because W&I policies exclude known matters.

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification only, on the Seller's reading. Our counsel should confirm against the lease text, including any change-in-control termination right. Add a covenant that the Seller gives notice on time.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the cover-note characterisations.** Bluefen is not "addressed", Riverlark is not debt-free, and DD-006 and Sandbar are unsupported. Require warranties if the Seller wants us to rely on them.
2. **Riverlark:** payoff letter, repayment from the price, and deed of release plus PPSR discharges *at* Completion. Payout defined as Indebtedness. Waiver of cl 8.1.
3. **Bluefen:** unconditional consent and cl 11.3 satisfied as a Buyer-only waivable CP. Best or all reasonable endeavours. Long-stop date. Consider price protection.
4. **Limitations:** apply only to general Warranty Claims. Carve out fraud, Fundamental and Tax Warranties, indemnities, covenants and leakage. Reverse the cl 12.3 default.
5. **Delete cl 8.3 and the general disclosures.** Specific, fair disclosure only. No disclosure against Fundamental or Tax Warranties or indemnities. Bring-down at Completion with no cure.
6. **Title and Capacity:** fundamental, 100% cap, 6–7 years. Independent title checks and Completion deliverables.
7. **Ironquay:** payment evidence plus confirmatory assignment at Completion. Otherwise a full uncapped IP indemnity with retention.
8. **DD-006:** information request now, pre-Completion NDB covenant, specific indemnity and retention. Flag the possibly missed 30-day assessment deadline.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus all on-costs treated as Transaction Costs, deducted from the price. Correct the funds flow.
10. **Sandbar:** diligence the split renewals. Treat them as one contract. Price or terminate if not genuinely ordinary course.
11. **Tax:** standalone tax indemnity and a separate limitation regime.
12. **Economics:** tipping basket, a modest de minimis, a 24-month time limit. Either a higher cap or 20% only with full carve-outs. Consider W&I insurance.
13. **Updated Disclosure Letter** as at a current date, plus a retention or escrow to back the specific indemnities.

**Caveats:** This review is based only on the Seller's cover note and Disclosure Letter. We have not seen the full SPA text or the underlying DD documents (DD-002 to DD-012). The clause readings above should be checked against those documents. Statutory rates and thresholds (payroll tax, super guarantee, NDB timing) should be confirmed by the relevant specialists before we rely on figures.
